title: Children of the Day
subtitle: 1 & 2 Thessalonians in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Paul's letters to the Thessalonians were written to a young church in a busy Macedonian port, only months after it began. They hold a household shrine left empty, a mother holding a child, a tentmaker working by lamplight so no one has to feed him, a friend sent back over the road with news, a grave visited with hope, and a lamp kept burning through the night.

This book walks through them in thirty-six short poems, in five parts: three for the first letter and two for the second. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things the letters touch—a lamp, a loom, a loaf of bread, a road at dawn—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the letters to the Thessalonians alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: three things remembered
paintings.epigraph: “your work of faith and labor of love and perseverance of hope”
paintings.poem:
Paul didn't remember
their doctrine first.

he remembered
what their faith did with its hands,
what their love
was tired from,
what their hope
kept standing up under.

faith that works.
love that labors.
hope that holds on.

he prayed it back to God
like a list of small gifts.

someone may be praying yours
right now.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “three things remembered” (1 Thessalonians 1:2–3)—where the poem notes, “someone may be praying yours right now”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: not in word only
paintings.epigraph: “our Good News came to you not in word only, but also in power”
paintings.poem:
words came first.
they always do.

but something else
came through the door with them,

the way warmth
comes in with bread,

the way a room changes
when the one you've waited for
steps inside.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from 1 Thessalonians 1:5 (“when the one you've waited for steps inside”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: affliction, with joy
paintings.epigraph: “having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit”
paintings.poem:
they didn't wait
for a better season
to believe.

the pressure came
the same week
as the good news.

and still
there was joy,
not instead of the trouble
but right there inside it,

a flower
in the crack of the wall
that was supposed to keep it out.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from 1 Thessalonians 1:6 (“in the crack of the wall that was supposed to keep it out”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: it went out from you
paintings.epigraph: “from you the word of the Lord has been declared”
paintings.poem:
nobody planned a campaign.

a sailor told a trader.
a trader told his wife
in another town.

the roads out of the city
carried olive oil and wool
and something new.

wherever Paul went next,
people had already heard.

a changed life
doesn't need
a messenger.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “it went out from you” (1 Thessalonians 1:8)—where the poem notes, “doesn't need a messenger”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: turned
paintings.epigraph: “you turned to God from idols, to serve a living and true God”
paintings.poem:
the little god in the wall niche
never heard a thing.
never needed anything
but dusting.

they turned
from what they had carried
to the One
who carries them.

from things
that stay where you set them

to a God
who is alive,
and true,
and moves toward you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “turned” (1 Thessalonians 1:9)—where the poem notes, “and true, and moves toward you”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: and to wait
paintings.epigraph: “to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead”
paintings.poem:
turning was the first half.

the second half
is waiting.

not the waiting
of a bus stop.

the waiting
of someone who has heard footsteps
on the road

and knows
whose they are.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In the quiet after the noise, what gentle truth from 1 Thessalonians 1:10 (“and knows whose they are”) is asking for your unhurried attention today?

paintings.title: bold, after Philippi
paintings.epigraph: “we grew bold in our God to tell you the Good News of God in much conflict”
paintings.poem:
they came in
with the bruises
from the last town
still on them.

any sensible man
would have kept quiet
for a while.

but boldness
wasn't something
they had.

it was something
they grew,
in God,

the way a bruise heals
from the inside.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “bold, after Philippi” (1 Thessalonians 2:2)—where the poem notes, “the way a bruise heals from the inside”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: like a nursing mother
paintings.epigraph: “But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishes her own children.”
paintings.poem:
he could have come in
with his title.

instead
he picked the gentlest picture
he knew:

a mother at night,
holding what she loves
close to the warmth,

not asking
what it will give her back.

this is what
the good news
looked like
in Thessalonica.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “like a nursing mother” (1 Thessalonians 2:7)—where the poem notes, “looked like in Thessalonica”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: our own souls
paintings.epigraph: “not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls”
paintings.poem:
you can hand someone a message
and keep your distance.

Paul didn't.

he gave the news
and then he gave
himself along with it,

the way you don't just
tell a hungry friend
where the bread is.

you sit down
and break yours.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “our own souls” (1 Thessalonians 2:8)—where the poem notes, “you sit down and break yours”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: night and day
paintings.epigraph: “working night and day, that we might not burden any of you”
paintings.poem:
by day, the needle
and the heavy cloth.

by lamplight, more needle.
more cloth.

and the good news,
perhaps to whoever
stopped by to talk.

he wanted no one
to wonder
what he was after.

so he paid
for his own bread,

and gave
the best thing he had
for free.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “night and day” (1 Thessalonians 2:9)—where the poem notes, “the best thing he had for free”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: as a father
paintings.epigraph: “as a father does his own children”
paintings.poem:
first a mother.
now a father.

Paul needed both
to say it:

tender enough to hold,
steady enough
to say walk this way.

encouraging.
comforting.
urging.

a hand around your hand
on the path,
until one day
you know the way yourself.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “as a father” (1 Thessalonians 2:11–12)—where the poem notes, “until one day you know the way yourself”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: you are our joy
paintings.epigraph: “For you are our glory and our joy.”
paintings.poem:
the athletes of his day
ran for a crown
of leaves.

Paul looked at a room
of workers and neighbors
and former idol-keepers

and said,
there it is.

that's my crown.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “you are our joy” (1 Thessalonians 2:19–20)—where the poem notes, “that's my crown”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: alone at Athens
paintings.epigraph: “we thought it good to be left behind at Athens alone”
paintings.poem:
he could have kept Timothy.
a friend at his side
in a strange city.

instead he sent him back
up the road,
to the people
he couldn't reach.

love sometimes looks like
choosing
to be the lonely one

so someone else
can be held.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “alone at Athens” (1 Thessalonians 3:1–2)—where the poem notes, “so someone else can be held”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: now we live
paintings.epigraph: “For now we live, if you stand fast in the Lord.”
paintings.poem:
all those weeks
Paul didn't know.

had the trouble
worn them down?
had they let go?

then Timothy,
dusty from the road,
with good news:

they're standing.
they miss you.

and the tired old apostle
said the most honest thing:

now we live.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “now we live” (1 Thessalonians 3:6–8)—where the poem notes, “now we live”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: abound
paintings.epigraph: “May the Lord make you to increase and abound in love toward one another”
paintings.poem:
he didn't pray
that their love
would be enough.

he prayed it would
run over.

a cup filled
past the rim,

spilling toward each other,
and then out the door,

toward all.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “abound” (1 Thessalonians 3:12)—where the poem notes, “toward all”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: with your own hands
paintings.epigraph: “that you make it your ambition to lead a quiet life, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands”
paintings.poem:
not the loudest life.
not the biggest.

a quiet one.

your own business,
done well.
your own hands,
tired in a good way.

ambition, Paul says,
but aimed low
and close:

a loom,
a table,
a neighbor who never wonders
if you're honest.

holiness
can look like this.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “with your own hands” (1 Thessalonians 4:11–12)—where the poem notes, “holiness can look like this”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: not like the rest
paintings.epigraph: “so that you don’t grieve like the rest, who have no hope”
paintings.poem:
Paul doesn't say
don't grieve.

he knows better.
tears are allowed.

he says
don't grieve
like there's no morning.

cry
with the door
left open.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Where is God inviting you to set down your work today and rest in what He has already finished (1 Thessalonians 4:13)?

paintings.title: fallen asleep
paintings.epigraph: “God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep in Jesus”
paintings.poem:
the church had a word
for the ones they'd lost.

not gone.
not ended.

asleep.

the word you use
for someone
you expect to see
at breakfast.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “fallen asleep” (1 Thessalonians 4:14)—where the poem notes, “you expect to see at breakfast”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: forever
paintings.epigraph: “So we will be with the Lord forever.”
paintings.poem:
a shout.
a trumpet.
the ones asleep first,

then everyone else,
gathered up
together.

we don't know
how.
Paul didn't pretend to.

he just told them
where the story ends:

with the Lord.
with each other.

not for a visit.

forever.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “forever” (1 Thessalonians 4:16–17)—where the poem notes, “forever”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: comfort one another
paintings.epigraph: “Therefore comfort one another with these words.”
paintings.poem:
he didn't write this
to win an argument
about the end of time.

he wrote it
so someone could say it
at a graveside.

read it out loud.
hold a hand.

that's what
it's for.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “comfort one another” (1 Thessalonians 4:18)—where the poem notes, “that's what it's for”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: a thief in the night
paintings.epigraph: “But you, brothers, aren’t in darkness, that the day should overtake you like a thief.”
paintings.poem:
a thief comes
to people who are asleep
with the lights out.

but you,
Paul says,
are children of the day.

the dark
isn't your address.

leave the lamp on.
you're expecting
someone you love.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “a thief in the night” (1 Thessalonians 5:4–5)—where the poem notes, “you're expecting someone you love”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: breastplate and helmet
paintings.epigraph: “putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet, the hope of salvation”
paintings.poem:
a soldier's gear
for people
who weren't soldiers.

faith and love
over the heart.

hope
around the head,

where the worry
likes to start.

stay awake.
stay dressed.

not for a battle.

for the morning.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “breastplate and helmet” (1 Thessalonians 5:8)—where the poem notes, “for the morning”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: always, without ceasing, in everything
paintings.epigraph: “Always rejoice. Pray without ceasing. In everything give thanks”
paintings.poem:
three short lines.
the shortest verses
in the letter.

rejoice.
pray.
give thanks.

not a schedule.
a flame you keep lit
while you do everything else.

kneading.
mending.
walking to the well.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “always, without ceasing, in everything” (1 Thessalonians 5:16–18)—where the poem notes, “mending. walking to the well”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: faithful
paintings.epigraph: “He who calls you is faithful, who will also do it.”
paintings.poem:
spirit, soul and body,
the whole of you,
kept whole.

it sounds like
too much to ask.

it is.

that's why
the last line
isn't about you.

the One who called
is faithful.

he'll finish
what he started.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “faithful” (1 Thessalonians 5:23–24)—where the poem notes, “he'll finish what he started”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: growing
paintings.epigraph: “your faith grows exceedingly, and the love of each and every one of you toward one another abounds”
paintings.poem:
the trouble
didn't stop.

neither did
the growing.

when Paul writes again,
and he can't help it:

your faith
is taller.

your love,
every one of you,
is wider.

some trees
put down the deepest roots
in the rockiest ground.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “growing” (2 Thessalonians 1:3)—where the poem notes, “put down the deepest roots in the rockiest ground”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: relief
paintings.epigraph: “to give relief to you who are afflicted with us”
paintings.poem:
they were tired
of being the ones
who suffered for being good.

Paul doesn't tell them
it doesn't matter.

he tells them
God sees,
and God is fair,

and when the Lord is revealed
there will be relief,

like cool water
at the end
of a long hot road.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “relief” (2 Thessalonians 1:6–7)—where the poem notes, “at the end of a long hot road”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: glorified in you
paintings.epigraph: “that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him”
paintings.poem:
glass doesn't
make the light.

it just
lets it through,

and somehow
it's more beautiful
for having been held.

his name in you.
you in him.

the light,
and the one
it shines through,

both shining.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “glorified in you” (2 Thessalonians 1:11–12)—where the poem notes, “both shining”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: not quickly shaken
paintings.epigraph: “not to be quickly shaken in your mind, and not be troubled”
paintings.poem:
rumors ran through the church:
a letter,
a voice,
someone who said
it's already over,
you missed it.

Paul wrote back.

no.
don't be shaken.
remember what I told you.

every age
has its alarm bells.

he still says
the same thing:

stay steady.
he hasn't forgotten you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “not quickly shaken” (2 Thessalonians 2:1–2)—where the poem notes, “stay steady. he hasn't forgotten you”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: chosen from the beginning
paintings.epigraph: “God chose you from the beginning for salvation”
paintings.poem:
before the dock,
before the loom,
before the idols in the wall,

before
they had anything
to offer,

God had chosen them.

and whatever loud voices
said about the end,

Paul pointed them
back to the beginning.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “chosen from the beginning” (2 Thessalonians 2:13)—where the poem notes, “Paul pointed them back to the beginning”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: good hope
paintings.epigraph: “gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace”
paintings.poem:
not a thin hope.
not a maybe.

good hope.

the kind that
keeps you warm
the way a banked fire does
through the night,

and is still there
in the morning
when you reach for it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “good hope” (2 Thessalonians 2:16–17)—where the poem notes, “in the morning when you reach for it”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: that the word may run
paintings.epigraph: “pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly”
paintings.poem:
the great apostle
asks the small church
to pray for him.

not for comfort.
for the word
to run.

the way news runs
down a road
ahead of the runner.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “that the word may run” (2 Thessalonians 3:1)—where the poem notes, “down a road ahead of the runner”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: the Lord is faithful
paintings.epigraph: “But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one.”
paintings.poem:
not all have faith,
Paul says.

and then,
almost in the same breath:

but the Lord
is faithful.

the world
can be unreliable.

he isn't.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “the Lord is faithful” (2 Thessalonians 3:3)—where the poem notes, “he isn't”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: into God's love
paintings.epigraph: “May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love, and into the perseverance of Christ.”
paintings.poem:
a heart
can wander off
in any direction.

so he prays
it will be steered,

like water
finding its way
downhill

into God's love,

and into the patience
of the One
who never
gave up on us.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: How does the mercy shown in “into God's love” (2 Thessalonians 3:5) change the way you look at your own weakness—or at someone who needs your grace today?

paintings.title: your own bread
paintings.epigraph: “that they work with quietness and eat their own bread”
paintings.poem:
some had stopped working.
the Lord was coming,
so why bother?

Paul's answer
was plain:

pick up your tools.
work quietly.
eat your own bread.

waiting well
looks a lot like
an ordinary workday,

done faithfully.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: How has God quietly provided enough for today’s road, and who might you welcome to your table in kindness (2 Thessalonians 3:10–12)?

paintings.title: don't grow weary
paintings.epigraph: “But you, brothers, don’t be weary in doing what is right.”
paintings.poem:
good is heavy
some days.

the same kindness,
the same work,
the same prayer,
and nothing seems to move.

don't be weary,
he says.

not because
it's easy.

because it's right.

and because
the One you're doing it for
is coming.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “don't grow weary” (2 Thessalonians 3:13)—where the poem notes, “the One you're doing it for is coming”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?

paintings.title: in my own hand
paintings.epigraph: “Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways.”
paintings.poem:
at the end
he takes the pen
from the one writing for him,

and adds a line
in his own hand,

so they'll know
it's really him.

peace,
he writes.

at all times.
in all ways.

the Lord
be with you all.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As you linger with “in my own hand” (2 Thessalonians 3:16–17)—where the poem notes, “the Lord be with you all”—where do you recognize this same moment on your own walk today?
